rationale: Excluded under E07 (wrong service). The study examines cross-sectoral and vertical institutional coordination in Zambia's water-land-food nexus, specifically focusing on the expansion of agricultural irrigation and the planning and licensing of large-scale public-private agricultural investment projects rather than household or community drinking water or sanitation service access.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type Criterion 2 reading and the literal/plain Criterion 2 wording yield an exclude verdict because the study clearly fails Criterion 1 (wrong service: agricultural irrigation and water-land-food nexus rather than household or community water/sanitation service access) and Criterion 4 (no household/community WASH access outcome). While the abstract examines institutional coordination, agricultural investment licensing, and customary-versus-statutory land tenure (satisfying plain Criterion 2 governance/institutional factors in the abstract), none of these mechanisms govern household or community water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: The focus of the study is the planning and licensing process of large-scale public-private agricultural investment projects with water/irrigation infrastructure as major components.
For this reason, the Zambian Government has planned the gradual expansion of irrigated areas throughout the country to boost agricultural production and productivity to meet domestic food demands

The study analyses the modes at hand to coordinate activities of more or less independent public-sector units related to agricultural development activities, the kind of coordination problems and the barriers and hindrances to effective coordination.
